solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What's suffered, say, by the Light Blues when preparing for battle?

parts.note: Cambridge University teams are the Light Blues, and the Cam is the river that runs through Cambridge

indicators.note: say tells us the word for suffering is only spoken, and the letters are spelt another way

parts.note: what you suffer is pain

explanation.surface: A rowing crew from Cambridge going through agony as they get ready for a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' means PAIN is only heard: it gives PAIGN, the same sound spelt another way. Cambridge sports teams are the 'Light Blues'; the Cam is the city's river. The blog points out the river is a stretch for the university.
explanation.definitionFit: A military operation made up of a series of engagements is called a campaign, so a battle stands for it loosely.

clue.text: Dream fairy's a nut on the internet

parts.note: a cob is a hazelnut, as in cobnut
the web is the internet

explanation.surface: A fairy from a play who is crazy about going online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dream' is Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, where one of Titania's fairies has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, one of the fairies attending Titania carries this name.

clue.text: Spray, sir?

definitions.meaning: a device with a fine nozzle for misting houseplants
the formal title for a man, used when addressing him

explanation.surface: A shop assistant offering a man a squirt of something.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a plant sprayer that produces fine droplets; the other is the courtesy title for a man, like sir.

clue.text: In essence, a precept raised under Tony Blair's leadership …

indicators.note: under puts the raised piece below the initials in this down answer
leadership asks for the leading letter of each of the two names
in a down clue, raised means the word for precept is written upwards

parts.note: a motto is a guiding rule or precept

explanation.surface: A political maxim promoted while Tony Blair led the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns MOTTO upwards to give OTTOM. 'leadership' takes T and B, the initials of Tony Blair, and 'under' puts OTTOM below them.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is true at bottom means it is true fundamentally, which is what in essence means.

clue.text: … crystallizes during meeting elsewhere

indicators.note: during says the letters sit inside the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Something takes firm shape while a gathering happens somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'meeting' into the start of 'elsewhere'.
explanation.definitionFit: When ideas or a plan crystallize they take definite form, just as a mixture sets firm.

clue.text: Sailor's pride perhaps injured

parts.note: pride is one of the seven deadly sins, so it is an example of a sin
an injured leg is a bad leg

explanation.surface: A seaman's self-respect may have taken a knock.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of the Arabian Nights who made seven voyages is the famous mariner of that name.

clue.text: Feed in flat?

parts.note: FE is the chemical symbol for iron, so FEED read as FE-ED gives the metal's name with ED; the result means pressed flat

explanation.surface: Giving someone a meal in an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feed' is read as FE, the symbol for iron, followed by ED. Spell out the metal's name and you get a word for pressed flat. The blog commenters noted that nothing in the clue signals the swap.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that have been pressed with a hot iron have been made flat and smooth.

clue.text: A beret — right in fashion -– is worn on the head

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means to shape, so these letters are shaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A beret with the right styling looks good on your head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fashion' tells you to rearrange A BERET plus RT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar-shaped clip that holds hair in place, so it is something worn on the head.

clue.text: One's French no good after dire upset involving second son

indicators.note: after puts the abbreviation for no good at the end
involving means the scrambled letters wrap around the two abbreviations
upset means the letters of the word dire are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A Frenchman reckoned useless after a disastrous mess-up concerning a younger child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges DIRE to DREI, and 'involving' puts SS inside it. The definition is cryptic: one type of this is French, as in salad.
explanation.definitionFit: French is one well-known variety of the oil-and-vinegar sauce poured over salad, so one of them is French.

clue.text: Game for a knees-up on station?

parts.note: a base is a station, a place where people are posted
a knees-up is British slang for a lively party, and a ball is a dance party

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture for a party held at a military station.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'knees-up' is British slang for a noisy party or dance.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the American bat-and-ball sport played on a diamond, so it is a game.

clue.text: Shell out for wire after herd's stragglers escape

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters behind the cut-down herd
the stragglers are the trailing letters, which run away and leave only the front of the word

parts.note: a herd is cows, the possessive read as plural

indicators.note: out means the letters of wire are put out of order

explanation.surface: Pay up for fencing wire once the last cattle have broken free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell out' looks like a phrase for paying; only 'Shell' is the definition. 'stragglers escape' removes WS from COWS, leaving CO; 'out' rearranges WIRE to WRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy sea snail whose shell was once used as money in Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Type of runner?

definitions.meaning: a typewriter-style typeface with fixed-width letters
a messenger who carries documents or parcels

explanation.surface: Asking what sort of athlete someone is.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a monospaced typeface; the other is someone who delivers messages, a runner in the old sense.

clue.text: Permits unplanned sex with tea

indicators.note: something unplanned is disordered, so the letters of the two words fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Lets spontaneous intimacy happen alongside a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unplanned' rearranges SEX and TEA together.
explanation.definitionFit: Boarding schools and colleges grant leave of absence on a written pass, so such passes are permits.

clue.text: Pony's shanks, all told, or only enough for Shanks's pony?

definitions.text: Pony's shanks, all told, or only enough for Shanks's pony?

parts.words: Pony's shanks, all told, or only enough for Shanks's pony?
parts.note: a pony's limbs counted up sound like four of them, while the front pair alone would be enough for walking on two feet

explanation.surface: A riddle about how many legs a pony has compared with going on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shanks's pony' is British slang for walking on your own legs. A pony's legs 'all told' number four, which sounds like the answer, and its front pair is enough for a two-legged walker.
explanation.definitionFit: The front limbs of a four-legged animal such as a pony are the ones at the front.

clue.text: Used to be into fish — withdrew

indicators.note: into puts the past form of be inside the fish

parts.note: a cod is a fish
were is a past form of be

explanation.surface: Someone who was once fond of fishing pulled back.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink back in fear is to recoil or draw away, so cowered fits withdrew.

clue.text: Time digesting Old Norse achieves higher degree

indicators.note: digesting means swallowing, so the word for time takes the language abbreviation inside it

parts.note: hours are a measure of time

explanation.surface: Years spent studying an old Scandinavian language earn an advanced qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'achieves' is a link. In Britain an honours degree ranks above an ordinary pass degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A British bachelor's degree with honours ranks above an ordinary pass, so it is a higher grade of degree.

clue.text: College on the up, except in English?

indicators.note: on the up means rising, so the two pieces are read backwards; the blog notes this suits a down clue better

parts.note: not as in all not, meaning except

explanation.surface: A school rising in the rankings, except perhaps in its English teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the up' reverses NOT E to give the college. The blog notes that 'up' suits a down clue better than this across one.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous English public school near Windsor is formally named a college.

clue.text: No IT at Oriel? Given this, the solution may be obvious

definitions.text: No IT at Oriel? Given this, the solution may be obvious

parts.words: No IT at Oriel? Given this, the solution may be obvious
parts.note: the first eight letters of the opening words, turned right round, spell the answer, so turning them makes it obvious

explanation.surface: A grumble that an Oxford college lacks computing, with a hint that the answer is easy.
explanation.walkthrough: Turn round the first eight letters of 'No IT at Oriel', NOITATOR, and you get the answer itself. Oriel is an Oxford college.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning something round, a full turn, is what the word names, and doing it to the letters reveals the solution.

clue.text: Twisting staircase adult's going to find most creepy

indicators.note: twisting means the letters of staircase are wound into a new order
going means the letter for adult departs from the mix

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for adult, a film certificate

explanation.surface: A spiral staircase, once the grown-up has gone, is the spookiest place to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisting' rearranges STAIRCASE and 'going' takes out an A for adult, leaving eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scary is frightening or spooky, and the superlative is the most frightening of all.

clue.text: 'Sovereign' with Peter, say, in the saddle, is very impressive

parts.note: Peter is an example of a saint, abbreviated ST
a rider in the saddle is on the horse
a king is a sovereign

explanation.surface: A monarch riding alongside Peter makes a striking sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter, say' is a saint, the usual crossword source of ST. 'Stonking' is British slang; 'is' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for excellent or remarkable, as in a stonking performance.

clue.text: Jaguar, maybe? Not posh originally

indicators.note: not here means without, so the letter for posh is taken away

parts.note: an ounce is a wild cat (the snow leopard), so a big cat like a jaguar is in the same family
U stands for upper-class, hence posh

explanation.surface: A luxury car that was originally anything but upmarket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jaguar' looks like the British car maker but is the big cat. 'Not' removes U, the letter for upper-class, from OUNCE, the snow leopard.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at one time in the past, so it is a synonym of formerly or at first.

clue.text: Interval of calm between Pope's Day One and Day Five

indicators.note: between puts the word for calm in the middle of the two day abbreviations

parts.note: in the Gregorian calendar of Pope Gregory XIII, Sunday is the first day, abbreviated S
the fifth day is Thursday, abbreviated TH
calm water is even

explanation.surface: A peaceful break in the Vatican's week, from its first day to its fifth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pope's' points to the Gregorian calendar, set up by Pope Gregory XIII, in which the week starts on Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the gap spanning seven notes of the scale, such as C to B, is an interval.

clue.text: Jovial Jack's left eye …

indicators.note: left means departed, so the jack letter has gone from the word

parts.note: jocular means jovial, full of jokes
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: A cheerful sailor has lost an eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has': Jack has left. The blog calls the answer a facetious word for the eye, as in 'ocular' meaning the eye itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Used jokingly as a noun, the word for anything to do with sight can stand for the organ of sight itself.

clue.text: … is able to notice area across the pond

parts.note: can means is able to
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A one-eyed sailor can still make out a region overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across the pond' means over the Atlantic from Britain, in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen from Britain, North America lies over the Atlantic, and this country is there.

clue.text: States impression first articulated in survey

indicators.note: first puts the spoken piece before the abbreviation for the country
articulated means pronounced, so the word for impression is only heard and spelt another way

parts.note: a sense is an impression or feeling
US is the United States

explanation.surface: America's opinion is what gets stated first in an opinion poll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articulated' makes SENSE sound-only, giving CENS.
explanation.definitionFit: An official count of a population is a survey of it.

clue.text: Fliers engage second propulsion element

indicators.note: engage means take on board, so the crew word holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: an aircrew is the people who fly a plane

explanation.surface: Pilots hire a deputy to help drive an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A propeller on an aircraft is the part that drives it forward, so it is a propulsion element.

clue.text: Where to keep change of underwear, should the need arise?

definitions.text: Where to keep change of underwear
definitions.meaning: spare clothes are packed inside a suitcase
a phrase meaning as a precaution, if it becomes necessary

explanation.surface: Packing spare pants for emergencies.
explanation.definitionFit: One reading is inside a suitcase where spare clothes go; the other is the phrase meaning as a precaution or if necessary.

clue.text: Clever chaps need supplement with iodine

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, like a newspaper's colour supplement
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Bright men need a vitamin boost with added iodine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need' is a link. 'supplement' looks like a health pill but is a newspaper's magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: The wise men who followed the star to Bethlehem were learned men, hence clever chaps.

clue.text: Principles in SALT agenda oddly backed by international leader

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word international goes at the front
backed means the picked letters are read from the end towards the start
oddly picks the first, third, fifth and so on of the letters in the two words

explanation.surface: Values at stake in arms-limitation talks, with a world leader backing them.
explanation.walkthrough: SALT was the Strategic Arms Limitation Talks between the US and USSR. 'oddly' picks SLAED, and 'backed' reverses it to DEALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are the high standards and values a person lives by, so they are principles.

clue.text: LONDON and PARIS?

parts.note: the two cities are each the seat of a national government, and the clue prints them in upper-case letters

explanation.surface: Two great European cities.
explanation.walkthrough: Both cities are seats of government, and the clue prints their names in upper case: two readings at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Both cities are the seats of their national governments, and the clue writes them in upper-case letters.

clue.text: Attorney spending time and energy redrafting

definitions.text: Attorney spending time and energy redrafting

indicators.note: redrafting means rewriting, so the remaining letters are put in a new order
spending means using up, so those two letters are taken away

explanation.surface: A lawyer putting effort and hours into rewriting a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spending' takes T and E out of ATTORNEY and 'redrafting' rearranges what is left. The whole clue describes a legal official at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer authorised to witness and certify documents, a kind of legal professional who drafts deeds.

clue.text: Australia's crazy but somewhat spellbinding batsman

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mesmerising Australian cricketer who is also a bit mad.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'but', which is the link joining the definition to the wordplay, so the definition is just 'Australia's crazy'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang, someone who is mad or eccentric is said to be dingbats.
